title: The top European cities in 2026
gist: Oxford Economics' 2026 Global Cities Index puts 44 European cities in the global top 100 (vs 34 for North America), with London second only to New York, Paris third, and Dublin and Zurich also in the top 10. Western Europe leads on Quality of Life, Environment and Governance but lags North America on Economics and Human Capital, while the faster-growing upside sits in 'Cities to Watch' (Manchester, Toulouse, Eindhoven, Warsaw, Tallinn), Prague, and high-growth, weaker-fundamentals cities such as Tirana, Chișinău and Antalya.

themes.theme: Europe's weight in the global city ranking

insights.claim: Europe holds 44 of the top 100 cities in Oxford Economics' 2026 Global Cities Index, ahead of North America with 34, which the index authors present as a challenge to the narrative of European decline.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: On composite city fundamentals Europe is not in decline; don't let the macro 'European decline' narrative push European urban real estate and location decisions down automatically.
insights.quote: Despite all the talk of European decline, the continent’s cities remain a dominant force on the global stage.

insights.claim: Western European cities score particularly highly on Quality of Life, Environment and Governance but slightly lag North American peers on Economics and Human Capital, while Eastern European cities are less advanced but faster-growing, scoring closer to Asian cities.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Western Europe is a quality and stability bet, not a growth bet; look to Eastern European cities for growth exposure, with fundamentals that are less developed.
insights.locator: European cities dominate the top 100 of our Global Cities Index

themes.theme: London, Paris and the global top 10

insights.claim: London ranks second in the 2026 Global Cities Index, just a fraction behind New York, and tops the global Human Capital category thanks to its universities, corporate headquarters and highly qualified workforce, while ranking seventh for Economics.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: London's lead in the talent pool supports its continued pull for HQ and professional-services location despite UK macro weakness.
insights.quote: London is just a fraction behind its transatlantic rival in second place
insights.locator: While New York leads the ranking

insights.claim: Paris ranks third globally in the 2026 Global Cities Index, with strong Human Capital and excellent Quality of Life, including the longest life expectancy of any city in the world.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Paris competes with London mainly on quality of life; that matters for attracting talent in relocation and office-demand decisions.
insights.locator: While New York leads the ranking

insights.claim: Dublin and Zurich complete Europe's presence in the global top 10: Dublin is one of Western Europe's most dynamic cities for GDP and employment growth with a very high Environment score, and Zurich ranks in the top 50 in four of the five categories, with high GDP per capita driven by a very productive mix of industries.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Dublin offers growth and Zurich offers breadth plus productivity; both are core Western European locations for high-value activity.
insights.locator: Dublin and Zurich are the other two European cities in the global top 10

insights.claim: Oslo, Stockholm and Copenhagen all rank in the global top 20 despite their smaller size, excelling on Environment and Governance because renewables dominate their energy mix, which gives them low emissions and high air quality, and because of strong institutions and favourable political and business environments.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Nordic cities show that the renewable energy mix and institutional quality raise a city's ranking; relevant to ESG-driven location decisions and allocations.

insights.claim: The top 10 European cities in the 2026 Global Cities Index are, in order: London, Paris, Dublin, Zurich, Oslo, Stockholm, Copenhagen, Munich, Amsterdam and Berlin.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: A reference list of core European urban markets; the German cities only enter at positions 8 and 10.
insights.locator: Top 10 European cities in 2026 Global Cities Index

insights.claim: Oxford Economics names Manchester, Toulouse, Eindhoven, Warsaw and Tallinn as 2026 'Cities to Watch': they are not necessarily top-ranked, but their fundamentals are improving rapidly.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: A watch list of second-tier European cities with improving fundamentals, useful for location selection and regional real-estate and infrastructure exposure.
insights.locator: In addition to established leaders, Europe also boasts some exciting challengers

insights.claim: Manchester has led UK growth in recent years by using a rapidly expanding professional services base, cultural heritage and more affordable housing to attract skilled professionals.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Cheaper housing relative to London is pulling talent to Manchester; supports regional UK office and residential demand outside the capital.
insights.locator: Manchester has been at the forefront of the UK’s growth

insights.claim: Toulouse and Eindhoven are cited as evidence that European manufacturing is not dead and that specialising in high-tech production can drive city-level success.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: European industrial decline is uneven: specialised high-tech manufacturing clusters are still gaining, so regional exposure should be picked by cluster rather than avoided wholesale.
insights.quote: Toulouse and Eindhoven have proved that European manufacturing is far from dead
insights.locator: Manchester has been at the forefront of the UK’s growth

themes.theme: Eastern Europe and Türkiye: growth vs fundamentals

insights.claim: Warsaw and Tallinn represent a dynamic group of Eastern European cities benefiting from strong investment and productivity growth.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Investment and productivity catch-up in CEE capitals is the growth engine to track for Eastern European urban exposure.
insights.locator: Warsaw and Tallinn are again different

insights.claim: Prague is the highest-ranked Eastern European city in the 2026 Global Cities Index, at 51st globally, combining high quality of life with robust forecast growth and a strong Governance score.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Prague offers CEE growth with Western-style quality of life and governance, making it one of the lower-risk growth locations in the region.
insights.locator: Prague is another strong candidate here

insights.claim: Some Eastern European cities, including Chișinău (Moldova), Tirana (Albania) and several Turkish cities, offer even stronger growth than the leading Eastern European cities but often lag on fundamental strengths.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: This is the high-growth, high-risk tier: higher growth comes with weaker institutions and infrastructure, so size positions accordingly.
insights.locator: There are other cities in the Eastern Europe group

insights.claim: Turkish cities benefit from much younger demographics than the rest of Europe; Istanbul ranks 64th in the Global Cities Index, and Antalya is highlighted as one of Türkiye's most dynamic cities.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Demographics give Turkish cities a structural growth edge over ageing Europe, pointing to secondary Turkish cities like Antalya as well as Istanbul.

insights.claim: Most Russian cities score poorly on both current fundamentals and future prospects in the 2026 Global Cities Index, with Moscow and St Petersburg only slightly better than the rest.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: The index sees no recovery case for Russian cities, even its main hubs.
insights.locator: In contrast, most Russian cities do not fare well
